fixes.explanation: Obey is the word, friend. God says, "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant…" (Jeremiah 11:3). Hearing them isn't enough, and neither is nodding along. The whole message hangs on that one word.

Once? Oh no, no, no, friend. God says, "…I strongly warned them again and again, saying, 'Obey My voice.'" (Jeremiah 11:7). Again and again is a long way from one time. That's a whole lot of warning from Egypt until that day.

False is right, friend. God says, "…I strongly warned them again and again, saying, 'Obey My voice.'" (Jeremiah 11:7). That's far more than once. The warnings stretched from the time of Egypt until that day.

Not the priests, friend. The verse says they "…will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense…" (Jeremiah 11:12). That's where the cry goes. The priests aren't in the verse at all.

Nope, that one's false, friend. The verse says "…these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:12). Certainly not, it says. So the gods they've been burning incense to won't be saving them.

Not this time, friend. God tells Jeremiah, "…do not pray for these people." (Jeremiah 11:14). He even adds that Jeremiah shouldn't raise up a cry or a prayer on their behalf. This one is a hard word for Jeremiah to carry.
True, friend. God says, "When you are wicked, then you rejoice." (Jeremiah 11:15). Those two things are put side by side in one sentence. It's a sad line to read.

That's the one, friend. The passage says, "But with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). The tree was once called flourishing and beautiful. That makes the fire a hard picture to look at.

Roots feel like a natural guess, since the tree was planted. But the passage goes another way. It says, "But with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). Fire is the picture here, friend.

Planted is right, friend. The verse says, "The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you…" (Jeremiah 11:17). He's the one who put them in the ground. That's why the olive tree picture fits together so well.
